Load row

November

Start, then build.

Weeks 1–5 of 26 · 2 Nov – 6 Dec

The plan starts on Monday 2 November.

Week 1 · Start. Record squat depth and choose working weights from recent sets. Test strict pull-ups, dips and push-ups on Thursday.

Week 2 · Build. Squat 4 × 5–6, sumo 3 × 4–5. Progress by completed reps. Flat and paused bench on Tuesday, volume bench and weighted dips on Saturday.

Week 3 · Build. Squat 4 × 5–6, sumo 3 × 4–5. Progress by completed reps. Flat and paused bench on Tuesday, volume bench and weighted dips on Saturday.

Week 4 · Build. Squat 4 × 5–6, sumo 3 × 4–5. Progress by completed reps. Flat and paused bench on Tuesday, volume bench and weighted dips on Saturday.

Week 5 · Build. Squat 4 × 5–6, sumo 3 × 4–5. Progress by completed reps. Flat and paused bench on Tuesday, volume bench and weighted dips on Saturday.

December

Build, then an easier week.

Weeks 6–9 of 26 · 7 Dec – 3 Jan

Week 6 · Build. Squat 4 × 5–6, sumo 3 × 4–5. Progress by completed reps. Flat and paused bench on Tuesday, volume bench and weighted dips on Saturday.

Week 7 · Build. Squat 4 × 5–6, sumo 3 × 4–5. Progress by completed reps. Flat and paused bench on Tuesday, volume bench and weighted dips on Saturday.

Week 8 · Build. Squat 4 × 5–6, sumo 3 × 4–5. Progress by completed reps. Flat and paused bench on Tuesday, volume bench and weighted dips on Saturday.

Week 9 · Easier week. Reduce barbell work and repeat the Thursday bodyweight benchmarks.

January

Strength work and a first practice single for each primary lift.

Weeks 10–13 of 26 · 4 Jan – 31 Jan

Week 10 · Strength. Squat 4 × 3–4 and sumo 3 × 3–4. Keep Tuesday flat and paused bench. Add one easy practice single per primary lift in weeks 12 and 16. Resume Thursday incline from week 8.

Week 11 · Strength. Squat 4 × 3–4 and sumo 3 × 3–4. Keep Tuesday flat and paused bench. Add one easy practice single per primary lift in weeks 12 and 16.

Week 12 · Strength. Before your regular squat, bench and sumo work, take one practice single per lift near RPE 7. Log each separately.

Week 13 · Strength. Squat 4 × 3–4 and sumo 3 × 3–4. Keep Tuesday flat and paused bench. Add one easy practice single per primary lift in weeks 12 and 16.

February

Strength work, a second practice single for each primary lift, then an easier week.

Weeks 14–17 of 26 · 1 Feb – 28 Feb

Week 14 · Strength. Squat 4 × 3–4 and sumo 3 × 3–4. Keep Tuesday flat and paused bench. Add one easy practice single per primary lift in weeks 12 and 16.

Week 15 · Strength. Squat 4 × 3–4 and sumo 3 × 3–4. Keep Tuesday flat and paused bench. Add one easy practice single per primary lift in weeks 12 and 16.

Week 16 · Strength. Before your regular squat, bench and sumo work, take one practice single per lift near RPE 7. Log each separately.

Week 17 · Easier week. Reduce barbell work and repeat the Thursday bodyweight benchmarks.

March

One working single on each main lift, followed by back-off sets.

Weeks 18–22 of 26 · 1 Mar – 4 Apr

Week 18 · Heavy. Each primary lift gets one working single and back-offs. Earn each 5 kg increase on two comparable training weeks. Resume Thursday incline from week 16.

Week 19 · Heavy. Each primary lift gets one working single and back-offs. Earn each 5 kg increase on two comparable training weeks.

Week 20 · Heavy. Each primary lift gets one working single and back-offs. Earn each 5 kg increase on two comparable training weeks.

Week 21 · Heavy. Each primary lift gets one working single and back-offs. Earn each 5 kg increase on two comparable training weeks.

Week 22 · Heavy. Each primary lift gets one working single and back-offs. Earn each 5 kg increase on two comparable training weeks.

April

Heavy practice, opener rehearsal, taper and test week.

Weeks 23–26 of 26 · 5 Apr – 2 May

Week 23 · Heavy. Each primary lift gets one working single and back-offs. Earn each 5 kg increase on two comparable training weeks.

Week 24 · Opener rehearsal. Rehearse familiar openers at RPE 7–8. Reduce back-offs and Thursday incline work.

Week 25 · Taper. Light, fast work. squat 105 kg for 2 × 2, bench 80 kg for 3 × 2, sumo 130 kg for 2 × 2. Thursday incline is one easy set of eight.Light, fast work. squat 100 kg for 2 × 2, bench 75 kg for 3 × 2, sumo 125 kg for 2 × 2. Thursday incline is one easy set of eight.Light, fast work. squat 110 kg for 2 × 2, bench 85 kg for 3 × 2, sumo 135 kg for 2 × 2. Thursday incline is one easy set of eight.

Week 26 · Test week. Squat Monday, bench Tuesday, recovery Wednesday, sumo Thursday, recovery Friday and bodyweight tests Saturday. Log results Sunday.

Monday 2 November · Week 1 · Lower A

Squat

About 70 min

1

Mobility warm-up

Before the first lift

  • Easy bike or walk3 min
  • Knee-to-wall ankle rocks2 × 10 per side
  • Adductor rock-backs× 10
  • Goblet squat hold at your depth2 × 20–30 s
  • Hip-hinge drill× 8

Mobility baseline. After the easy bike or walk and before stretching, record the comfortable fingertip-to-floor gap in cm and knee-to-wall distance in cm for each ankle. Use the same stance and setup each time. Film a scheduled squat warm-up from the side at your usual depth and camera angle.

2

Before your first squat

Week 1 only

Film from the side with an empty bar and at 60 kg if comfortable. Record the deepest repeatable squat you can control. For the listed squat test standard, the hip crease reaches the top of the knee or lower. If heel elevation helps, use lifting shoes or a stable heel wedge. Keep foot support and depth consistent when comparing results.

4

Paused sumo

Second session · Normal row · Lighter row · Heavier row

Warm-up in kg · 60 × 5 · 70 × 260 × 560 × 5 · 75 × 2

  1. Set 1908095kg×3
  2. Set 2908095kg×3

Two easy technique sets. Pause for one second just off the floor, reset every rep and leave at least three clean reps in reserve. Rest 2–3 minutes. Use an easier row or one set if Monday fatigue carries into the main sumo session. These sets do not earn load increases.

Lighter80 kg × 3, 3Warm-up 60 × 5
Normal90 kg × 3, 3Warm-up 60 × 5 · 70 × 2
Heavier95 kg × 3, 3Warm-up 60 × 5 · 75 × 2
5

Accessories

Choose the weight by feel

  • Leg extension2 × 10–151 left · rest 90 s. Pad just above the ankle, knee in line with the machine pivot.
  • Seated leg curl2 × 8–121 left · rest 90 s. Hips back in the seat; brief squeeze with the knees bent. Use the lying leg curl only if this one is taken; the seated one grows the hamstrings more.
  • Standing calf raise2 × 8–121 left · rest 60–90 s. Smith machine or leg-press calf raise; pause 1–2 s in the bottom stretch.
6

Stretch

  • Half-kneeling hip flexor2 × 30 s per side
  • Frog inner-thigh stretch2 × 45 s
  • Wall calf stretch2 × 30 s per side

Accessories

Accessories

Choose the weight by feel

  • Bulgarian split squat2 × 8–12 per leg2 left · rest 2 min. Rear foot on a bench, dumbbells at your sides; straps if grip fades.
  • Leg press2 × 10–151–2 left · rest 2 min. Lower until just before your pelvis starts to roll off the pad. If it's taken, use the hack squat for the same reps, with your heels down and your lower back on the pad.
  • Seated calf raise machine2 × 12–201 left · rest 60 s. Pause 1–2 s in the bottom stretch; no bouncing.
  • Hip abduction machine2 × 12–201 left · rest 60 s. Sit tall, push your knees out, pause 1 s with your legs wide, then return slowly.
  • Hip adduction machine2 × 10–151–2 left · rest 60–90 s. Start as wide as is comfortable, squeeze the pads together, then open slowly without bouncing.

Thursday 5 November · Week 1 · Upper B

Bodyweight benchmarks

About 55 min

1

Bodyweight tests

In this order, 5 minutes apart

  1. Pull-upsDead hang, chin over the barMax reps
  2. DipsYour usual depth, full lockoutMax reps
  3. Push-upsChest to a fist-height markerMax reps

Log clean reps and bodyweight. Keep the same test order at each benchmark. These single-set tests take the place of Thursday’s incline work.

2

Accessories

Choose the weight by feel

  • Reverse pec deck2 × 12–201 left · rest 60–90 s. Open the arms without shrugging.
  • Incline or preacher curl2 × 8–121 left · rest 90 s. Incline with dumbbells, or preacher on the bench or the cable preacher. Upper arm still; lower under control.
  • Pallof press2 × 10–12 per siderest 60 s. Stand side-on to the cable, press straight out and resist turning.
  • Wrist curl2 × 12–201 left · rest 60 s. Forearms on a bench or the forearm cable machine, palms up; let the handle roll down to your fingers, then curl your wrists up.
  • Reverse wrist curl2 × 12–201 left · rest 60 s. Straight after the wrist curl, palms down; lift the backs of your hands, then lower slowly.
3

Stretch

6–8 minutes, after the session

Low-incline bench press

Two work sets · 2 clean reps left

Use a 30° bench. Warm up with 20 kg × 8 for working weights of 25 kg or more. Add 30 kg × 5 when working at 35 kg or above.

  1. Set 18–12reps
  2. Set 28–12reps

Working weight. First session, try 45 kg total. Use 40 kg if eight clean reps at 45 kg would leave fewer than two in reserve. On later Thursdays, use your last regular working weight. Once both sets reach 12 at the same load with at least two clean reps left, use the next 5 kg step at the next regular session and aim for eight per set.

Barbell steps and setup

20 · 25 · 30 · 35 · 40 · 45 · 50 · 55 · 60 · 65 · 70 kg. Continue in 5 kg steps. All weights include the bar. For work at 50 kg or above, an extra 1–3 warm-up reps one step below your working weight can help you judge today’s load.

Use safeties or a spotter. Keep your feet planted and your back comfortably supported. Use the same bench setting and controlled range each week. Rest 2–3 minutes between work sets.

If a new weight works for the first eight but is too heavy for the second set, use the previous weight for set two. Log both loads and both rep counts.

Low-incline bench press

Two work sets · 2 clean reps left

  1. Set 18–12reps
  2. Set 28–12reps

Working weight. First session, try 45 kg total. Use 40 kg if eight clean reps at 45 kg would leave fewer than two in reserve. On later Thursdays, use your last regular working weight. Once both sets reach 12 at the same load with at least two clean reps left, use the next 5 kg step at the next regular session and aim for eight per set.

Barbell steps and setup

20 · 25 · 30 · 35 · 40 · 45 · 50 · 55 · 60 · 65 · 70 kg. Continue in 5 kg steps. All weights include the bar. For work at 50 kg or above, an extra 1–3 warm-up reps one step below your working weight can help you judge today’s load.

Use safeties or a spotter. Keep your feet planted and your back comfortably supported. Use the same bench setting and controlled range each week. Rest 2–3 minutes between work sets.

If a new weight works for the first eight but is too heavy for the second set, use the previous weight for set two. Log both loads and both rep counts.

Low-incline bench press

Two work sets · 2 clean reps left

Use a 30° bench. Warm up with 20 kg × 8 for working weights of 25 kg or more. Add 30 kg × 5 when working at 35 kg or above.

  1. Set 18–12reps
  2. Set 28–12reps

Working weight. First session, try 45 kg total. Use 40 kg if eight clean reps at 45 kg would leave fewer than two in reserve. On later Thursdays, use your last regular working weight. Once both sets reach 12 at the same load with at least two clean reps left, use the next 5 kg step at the next regular session and aim for eight per set.

Barbell steps and setup

20 · 25 · 30 · 35 · 40 · 45 · 50 · 55 · 60 · 65 · 70 kg. Continue in 5 kg steps. All weights include the bar. For work at 50 kg or above, an extra 1–3 warm-up reps one step below your working weight can help you judge today’s load.

Use safeties or a spotter. Keep your feet planted and your back comfortably supported. Use the same bench setting and controlled range each week. Rest 2–3 minutes between work sets.

If a new weight works for the first eight but is too heavy for the second set, use the previous weight for set two. Log both loads and both rep counts.

Two work sets · 2 clean reps left

  1. Set 18–12reps

Working weight. First session, try 45 kg total. Use 40 kg if eight clean reps at 45 kg would leave fewer than two in reserve. On later Thursdays, use your last regular working weight. Once both sets reach 12 at the same load with at least two clean reps left, use the next 5 kg step at the next regular session and aim for eight per set.

Barbell steps and setup

20 · 25 · 30 · 35 · 40 · 45 · 50 · 55 · 60 · 65 · 70 kg. Continue in 5 kg steps. All weights include the bar. For work at 50 kg or above, an extra 1–3 warm-up reps one step below your working weight can help you judge today’s load.

Use safeties or a spotter. Keep your feet planted and your back comfortably supported. Use the same bench setting and controlled range each week. Rest 2–3 minutes between work sets.

If a new weight works for the first eight but is too heavy for the second set, use the previous weight for set two. Log both loads and both rep counts.

Barbell steps and setup

20 · 25 · 30 · 35 · 40 · 45 · 50 · 55 · 60 · 65 · 70 kg. Continue in 5 kg steps. All weights include the bar. For work at 50 kg or above, an extra 1–3 warm-up reps one step below your working weight can help you judge today’s load.

Working weight. First session, try 45 kg total. Use 40 kg if eight clean reps at 45 kg would leave fewer than two in reserve. On later Thursdays, use your last regular working weight. Once both sets reach 12 at the same load with at least two clean reps left, use the next 5 kg step at the next regular session and aim for eight per set. Barbell steps and setup

20 · 25 · 30 · 35 · 40 · 45 · 50 · 55 · 60 · 65 · 70 kg. Continue in 5 kg steps. All weights include the bar. For work at 50 kg or above, an extra 1–3 warm-up reps one step below your working weight can help you judge today’s load.

Use safeties or a spotter. Keep your feet planted and your back comfortably supported. Use the same bench setting and controlled range each week. Rest 2–3 minutes between work sets.

If a new weight works for the first eight but is too heavy for the second set, use the previous weight for set two. Log both loads and both rep counts.

Low-incline bench press

Two work sets · 2 clean reps left

Use a 30° bench. Warm up with 20 kg × 8 for working weights of 25 kg or more. Add 30 kg × 5 when working at 35 kg or above.

  1. Set 18–12reps
  2. Set 28–12reps

Working weight. First session, try 45 kg total. Use 40 kg if eight clean reps at 45 kg would leave fewer than two in reserve. On later Thursdays, use your last regular working weight. Once both sets reach 12 at the same load with at least two clean reps left, use the next 5 kg step at the next regular session and aim for eight per set.

Barbell steps and setup

20 · 25 · 30 · 35 · 40 · 45 · 50 · 55 · 60 · 65 · 70 kg. Continue in 5 kg steps. All weights include the bar. For work at 50 kg or above, an extra 1–3 warm-up reps one step below your working weight can help you judge today’s load.

Use safeties or a spotter. Keep your feet planted and your back comfortably supported. Use the same bench setting and controlled range each week. Rest 2–3 minutes between work sets.

If a new weight works for the first eight but is too heavy for the second set, use the previous weight for set two. Log both loads and both rep counts.

Two work sets · 2 clean reps left

Use a 30° bench. Warm up with 20 kg × 8 for working weights of 25 kg or more. Add 30 kg × 5 when working at 35 kg or above.

  1. Set 18–12reps

Working weight. First session, try 45 kg total. Use 40 kg if eight clean reps at 45 kg would leave fewer than two in reserve. On later Thursdays, use your last regular working weight. Once both sets reach 12 at the same load with at least two clean reps left, use the next 5 kg step at the next regular session and aim for eight per set.

Barbell steps and setup

20 · 25 · 30 · 35 · 40 · 45 · 50 · 55 · 60 · 65 · 70 kg. Continue in 5 kg steps. All weights include the bar. For work at 50 kg or above, an extra 1–3 warm-up reps one step below your working weight can help you judge today’s load.

Use safeties or a spotter. Keep your feet planted and your back comfortably supported. Use the same bench setting and controlled range each week. Rest 2–3 minutes between work sets.

If a new weight works for the first eight but is too heavy for the second set, use the previous weight for set two. Log both loads and both rep counts.

20 · 25 · 30 · 35 · 40 · 45 · 50 · 55 · 60 · 65 · 70 kg. Continue in 5 kg steps. All weights include the bar. For work at 50 kg or above, an extra 1–3 warm-up reps one step below your working weight can help you judge today’s load.

Low-incline bench press

Two work sets · 2 clean reps left

  1. Set 18–12reps
  2. Set 28–12reps

Working weight. First session, try 45 kg total. Use 40 kg if eight clean reps at 45 kg would leave fewer than two in reserve. On later Thursdays, use your last regular working weight. Once both sets reach 12 at the same load with at least two clean reps left, use the next 5 kg step at the next regular session and aim for eight per set.

Barbell steps and setup

20 · 25 · 30 · 35 · 40 · 45 · 50 · 55 · 60 · 65 · 70 kg. Continue in 5 kg steps. All weights include the bar. For work at 50 kg or above, an extra 1–3 warm-up reps one step below your working weight can help you judge today’s load.

Use safeties or a spotter. Keep your feet planted and your back comfortably supported. Use the same bench setting and controlled range each week. Rest 2–3 minutes between work sets.

If a new weight works for the first eight but is too heavy for the second set, use the previous weight for set two. Log both loads and both rep counts.

Low-incline bench press

Two work sets · 2 clean reps left

Use a 30° bench. Warm up with 20 kg × 8 for working weights of 25 kg or more. Add 30 kg × 5 when working at 35 kg or above.

  1. Set 18–12reps
  2. Set 28–12reps

Working weight. First session, try 45 kg total. Use 40 kg if eight clean reps at 45 kg would leave fewer than two in reserve. On later Thursdays, use your last regular working weight. Once both sets reach 12 at the same load with at least two clean reps left, use the next 5 kg step at the next regular session and aim for eight per set.

Barbell steps and setup

20 · 25 · 30 · 35 · 40 · 45 · 50 · 55 · 60 · 65 · 70 kg. Continue in 5 kg steps. All weights include the bar. For work at 50 kg or above, an extra 1–3 warm-up reps one step below your working weight can help you judge today’s load.

Use safeties or a spotter. Keep your feet planted and your back comfortably supported. Use the same bench setting and controlled range each week. Rest 2–3 minutes between work sets.

If a new weight works for the first eight but is too heavy for the second set, use the previous weight for set two. Log both loads and both rep counts.

Low-incline bench press

Two work sets · 2 clean reps left

Use a 30° bench. Warm up with 20 kg × 8 for working weights of 25 kg or more. Add 30 kg × 5 when working at 35 kg or above.

  1. Set 18–12reps
  2. Set 28–12reps

Working weight. First session, try 45 kg total. Use 40 kg if eight clean reps at 45 kg would leave fewer than two in reserve. On later Thursdays, use your last regular working weight. Once both sets reach 12 at the same load with at least two clean reps left, use the next 5 kg step at the next regular session and aim for eight per set.

Barbell steps and setup

20 · 25 · 30 · 35 · 40 · 45 · 50 · 55 · 60 · 65 · 70 kg. Continue in 5 kg steps. All weights include the bar. For work at 50 kg or above, an extra 1–3 warm-up reps one step below your working weight can help you judge today’s load.

Use safeties or a spotter. Keep your feet planted and your back comfortably supported. Use the same bench setting and controlled range each week. Rest 2–3 minutes between work sets.

If a new weight works for the first eight but is too heavy for the second set, use the previous weight for set two. Log both loads and both rep counts.

Barbell steps and setup

20 · 25 · 30 · 35 · 40 · 45 · 50 · 55 · 60 · 65 · 70 kg. Continue in 5 kg steps. All weights include the bar. For work at 50 kg or above, an extra 1–3 warm-up reps one step below your working weight can help you judge today’s load.

Squat and sumo progression. Start a new load at the bottom of its range. Complete the top reps on every set with at least two left on the last set at the same load twice. When progress slows. If three comparable main sessions stall or regress, review the training log, sleep, food, bodyweight, technique and secondary work before raising the load. For lower-body fatigue, reduce Monday’s two paused-sumo sets to one easy set or omit Friday’s optional back extension. For pressing, compare Tuesday bench and Saturday bench and dips at similar bodyweight, load and effort. If fatigue from Thursday persists over two comparable Saturdays, use one incline set until performance recovers.

Choosing weights at your gym

Barbells move in 5 kg steps · Belts move in 2.5 kg steps

Gym increments. All barbell numbers include the 20 kg bar. The smallest total change is 5 kg with one 2.5 kg plate on each side. A dip or pull-up belt can move in 2.5 kg steps.

Choosing a row. The Load row selector applies to both the Plan and Weights tabs. For each lift with preset rows, the workout shows the selected warm-up and sets. The other two rows appear below. Pick each lift’s weight from its own log. Use the additional load options on main squat and sumo days, and during the heavy block, when your working weight falls outside the three examples.

Starting an existing calendar. Use recent comparable sessions to choose your entry weight. Keep completed dates, sets, reps and effort in your own training log. This file remembers your place in the plan. Start a new phase at a load supported by your log. RPE 7, 8 and 9 correspond roughly to three, two and one additional clean reps in reserve.

Secondary barbell work. Use the Friday squat or Monday paused-sumo example matching the main lift’s row. If holding a weight outside the three examples, use the closest secondary row and keep it easy. Monday’s two paused-sumo sets finish with at least three clean reps left. Taper and test weeks omit them.

Belt lifts. Use the added kilograms in your log. Add one 2.5 kg plate on the next regular session after two comparable sessions at the same load when all reps are complete and at least four remain on the final set. In week 1, one qualifying session is enough. Otherwise hold. If you miss the reps or finish with less than one in reserve, reduce by 2.5 kg. Row labels may change between weeks. Record bodyweight alongside the belt load. A dip milestone is +25 kg for three clean sets of six at a consistent depth. If your earned belt load is outside next week’s examples, reuse a comfortable warm-up for that load and follow the day’s rep targets.

Low-incline bench. Follow the reps and weights in its own Weights tab. The Thursday session shows the current phase prescription.

Bodyweight work and low-incline bench

Thursday pressing and the four bodyweight benchmarks

  • Weeks 2–8, 10–16 and 18–23. Do pull-ups, strict push-ups and then 30° low-incline barbell bench for 2 × 8–12. On the bodyweight sets, follow the printed target and stop when one clean rep remains. Leave two on incline.
  • Weeks 24 and 25. Use one set of eight on incline. Leave at least three reps in week 24 and four in week 25.
  • Benchmark dates. In weeks 1, 9 and 17, test on Thursday. In week 26, test on Saturday after the three barbell tests. Do one strict set each of pull-ups, dips and push-ups in that order, five minutes apart. Record clean reps and bodyweight so the four tests are comparable.
  • Other accessories. Choose a weight that leaves the printed number of clean reps. When every set reaches the top of the range at that effort, move up one available increment.

Standards

The same on every rep.

  • Squat. For the listed test standard, the hip crease reaches the top of the knee or lower. Use your recorded depth and keep the whole foot supported. If you use lifting shoes or a stable heel wedge, keep that setup consistent.
  • Bench: touch the chest, no bounce, same grip; safeties set or a spotter.
  • Sumo: reset every rep on the floor, brace, push the floor away, stand tall without leaning back.
  • Pull-ups and dips: dead hang to chin over the bar; dips to the same depth every rep with full lockout.
  • Push-ups: chest to a fist-height marker, full lockout, body in one line.

Mobility

Before squat and sumo days, and after every session.

Before squat and sumo days

  • 3 minutes of easy cycling or walking.
  • Knee-to-wall ankle rocks, 2 × 10 per side. Adductor rock-backs, 10.
  • Goblet squat hold at your depth, 2 × 20–30 s. Hip-hinge drill, 8.

After training

  • All training days. Lying hamstring strap stretch, 2 × 45 s per side. Sunday stretching is optional.
  • Lower-body sessions. Half-kneeling hip flexor 2 × 30 s per side, frog inner-thigh stretch 2 × 45 s, and wall calf stretch 2 × 30 s per side. With the hamstring stretch, the holds total 8 min 30 s. Allow about 10–12 min with transitions.
  • Upper-body sessions. 90/90 hip switches × 8 and figure-4 glute stretch 2 × 30 s per side. Allow about 6–8 min with the hamstring stretch.

Mobility checkpoints

  • Measure on Monday in weeks 1, 5, 9, 13, 17, 21 and 26. The warm-up card includes both distances and a side-on squat video. Use the same conditions for each comparison.

Back care

For your L5–S1 history.

You report an L5–S1 disc bulge about three years ago and are currently largely symptom-free. These rules keep the plan sensible for that history; they are not a diagnosis or clearance.

  • Squat to the deepest point you can reach with your lower back neutral.
  • If ordinary back fatigue accumulates, reduce Monday’s two paused-sumo sets to one easy set or omit Friday’s optional back extension. Reassess how Wednesday’s main pulls feel.
  • New pain spreading down a leg, tingling, numbness or weakness: stop the exercise that provokes it and see a clinician.

Seek emergency care now

  • With back or leg symptoms, new difficulty passing or controlling urine, loss of bowel control, numbness around the genitals or saddle area, or severe and rapidly worsening leg weakness warrant emergency assessment.
NHS guidance on sciatica

Food and recovery

Eat to gain, sleep to recover.

  • Protein. Your reported intake is about 80 g daily. Aim first for around 110 g, about 30 g more per day. The plan’s working range is 110–120 g, spread across 3–5 meals.
  • Bodyweight. At 60 kg, the suggested weekly scale-weight trend is 0.15–0.30 kg. Sustained over all 26 weeks, that would be 3.9–7.8 kg. Start with about 300 extra kcal a day, weigh under similar conditions on 3–4 mornings per week and adjust intake by about 150–200 kcal if the three-week trend calls for it.
  • Creatine (optional). The plan’s dose is 3–5 g of creatine monohydrate daily. Early water-weight changes vary. Use weekly weight averages to judge your trend.
  • Sleep: keep your 7–9 hours. Alcohol: not the night before Monday or Wednesday.

Chest and shoulders. During regular training, two low-incline sets give the upper chest a dedicated pressing angle. The front delts and triceps assist the presses. The build week also has six direct cable lateral-raise sets, three reverse pec-deck sets and two overhead cable triceps-extension sets. Rows provide additional rear-delt work. A compound set can involve several muscles.

Bench and weighted dips. Bench still comes first on Tuesday and Saturday. Saturday’s belt-loaded dips follow volume bench. The swap takes total weekly dip sets from five to three in a build week and retains all three weighted sets. Record bodyweight, added weight, set reps and effort under the same conditions. One weekly dip practice gives you fewer chances to practise high-rep dips.

Fatigue. The old final dip set left about one rep. Incline leaves two, and strict push-ups now come first among Thursday’s presses. Push-up reps and soreness can change even with the same set count. If two comparable Saturdays show fewer bench or weighted-dip reps at similar load and effort, and Thursday fatigue is lingering, use one incline set with three reps left next training Thursday. Resume two sets once performance and recovery settle.

Lower-body recovery. Monday has two easy paused-sumo sets before Wednesday’s main pull. Friday’s squat stays secondary. Check whether either exposure affects the next main session. Test-week sumo moves to Thursday and bodyweight tests to Saturday.

Practice weeks. Weeks 12 and 16 each add one low-fatigue bench single near RPE 7. The other 16 pressing sets match an ordinary build or strength week. A single provides practice with a heavier weight and contributes less repeated-rep work than an incline or dip set.

Evidence behind the design

What the structure leans on.

  • A small training study in untrained men found greater upper-site chest growth with incline-only pressing. The mixed and flat-only groups had similar results. Chaves et al., 2020.
  • Heavier resistance training across at least two weekly sessions supports maximal strength. The bench targets and thresholds here are individual coaching choices. ACSM position stand, 2026.
  • Varying load and reps within the week favoured strength in trained lifters: Moesgaard et al., 2022.
  • Muscle growth improves as sets end closer to failure; strength gains are similar across a wide range of reps in reserve: Robinson et al., 2024.
  • Each muscle at least twice a week, heavy loads for strength, about 10 sets per muscle per week for growth: ACSM position stand, 2026.
  • Full squats grew the glutes and inner thighs more than half squats: Kubo et al., 2019.
  • Strength training improves range of motion about as much as stretching: Alizadeh et al., 2023; at least 5 minutes of stretching per muscle per week: Thomas et al., 2018.
  • Seated leg curls grew the hamstrings more than lying ones, 14% against 9%: Maeo et al., 2021.
  • Standing calf raises produced more gastrocnemius growth than seated raises in this study. Soleus growth was similar with both versions. Kinoshita et al., 2023.
  • Machines and free weights built similar muscle, while strength improved most on the tool that was trained: Haugen et al., 2023.
  • Overhead triceps extensions grew the triceps more than pushdowns, the long head most of all (28.5% against 19.6%): Maeo et al., 2023.
  • Bench pressing alone barely grew the triceps long head; adding triceps extensions did: Brandão et al., 2020.
  • Weight gain and protein targets for intermediate lifters: Iraki et al., 2019. Creatine safety: ISSN position stand. Review of creatine and water retention.

Choose a single near RPE 7 independently of the work weight. If a warm-up reaches that effort, count it and end the ramp.

Weeks 18–23. The Normal bench singles are 85 kg in weeks 18–19, 90 kg in weeks 20–21 and 95 kg in weeks 22–23 when earned.The Lighter bench singles are 80 kg in weeks 18–19, 85 kg in weeks 20–21 and 90 kg in weeks 22–23 when earned.The Heavier bench singles are 90 kg in weeks 18–19, 95 kg in weeks 20–21 and 100 kg in weeks 22–23 when earned. Take one working single per lift. Add 5 kg on a future main day after two comparable weeks at the same weight when both singles rate RPE 7.5 or easier, all back-offs are complete and the last back-off leaves at least two clean reps. At RPE 8–8.5 repeat the load. At RPE 9 or above reduce the next heavy-session weight by 5 kg. Choose a lighter single today if warm-ups feel unusually hard. Saturday follows the Tuesday single you completed.

Weeks 24 and 25. The Normal week 24 rehearsal is 90 kg. The week 25 main bench session is 80 kg for 3 × 2.The Lighter week 24 rehearsal is 85 kg. The week 25 main bench session is 75 kg for 3 × 2.The Heavier week 24 rehearsal is 95 kg. The week 25 main bench session is 85 kg for 3 × 2. Use a familiar opener at RPE 7–8. Rehearse 95 kg only when it already meets that standard. Keep taper doubles easy.

Readiness. 85 kg × 4 around RPE 8 in the strength block and 90 kg × 1 at RPE 7–7.5 or 95 kg × 1 at RPE 8–8.5 late in the program support considering the goal route.

Tuesday test. Use up to three singles and rest 4–6 minutes between attempts. Choose an opener recently completed cleanly at RPE 8 or easier. If warm-ups feel heavy, use the lighter route. 90 → 95 → 100 kg is the goal route. A 90 kg opener at RPE 9 ends the test. At RPE 8, consider 95 only if recent work supports it. Attempt 100 only after a clean 95 at about RPE 8–8.5 or easier with clear reserve. If 95 is a genuine RPE 9, finish there. Use 95 → 100 → 105 only when 95 is a reliably comfortable opener and 100 also leaves clear reserve. End the session after a miss, a grind, loss of your usual technique or concerning symptoms. Log the heaviest completed single.Lighter route: 85 → 90 → 95 kg. Choose 85 kg only if it has been a repeatable, clean single at RPE 8 or easier in recent training. Rest 4–6 minutes between attempts. If 85 kg is a genuine RPE 9 today, finish there. Take 90 kg only after a controlled opener and when recent work supports the increase. Attempt 95 kg only if 90 kg is clean, around RPE 8–8.5 or easier, with clear reserve. A genuine RPE 9 at 90 kg ends the test. End testing after a miss, a grind, loss of your usual technique or concerning symptoms. Record the heaviest successful single.Heavier route: 95 → 100 → 105 kg. Choose 95 kg only if it has been a repeatable, clean single at RPE 8 or easier in recent training. Rest 4–6 minutes between attempts. If 95 kg is a genuine RPE 9 today, finish there. Take 100 kg only after a controlled opener and when recent work supports the increase. Attempt 105 kg only if 100 kg is clean, around RPE 8–8.5 or easier, with clear reserve. A genuine RPE 9 at 100 kg ends the test. End testing after a miss, a grind, loss of your usual technique or concerning symptoms. Record the heaviest successful single.

Choose your sumo deadlift weights

Reported best 160 kg · Goal 175 kg · Stretch 180 kg

Build and strength. Working options are 115, 120, 125, 130, 135 kg for 3 × 4–5 in weeks 2–8, followed by 130, 135, 140, 145, 150 kg for 3 × 3–4 in weeks 10–16. Use the row your log supports. Start a new weight at the bottom of the rep range. Move up 5 kg on a future main day only after two comparable sessions at the same weight reach the top on every set, with at least two clean reps left on the final set both times. With one left, repeat. After a miss or a grind, use the next lighter load. Easier weeks and secondary work do not count.

Practice singles in weeks 12 and 16. The Normal examples are 150 kg in week 12 and 155 kg in week 16.The Lighter examples are 145 kg in week 12 and 150 kg in week 16.The Heavier examples are 155 kg in week 12 and 160 kg in week 16. Choose a single near RPE 7 independently of the work weight. If a warm-up reaches that effort, count it and end the ramp.

Heavy weeks. At RPE 8–8.5 repeat the load. At RPE 9 or above reduce the next heavy-session weight by 5 kg. Choose a lighter single today if warm-ups feel unusually hard. Week 24 uses reduced back-offs. Week 25 tapers.

Readiness. 145 kg × 4 around RPE 8 in the strength block and 160 kg × 1 at RPE 7–7.5 or 165 kg × 1 at RPE 8–8.5 late in the program support considering the goal route.

Thursday test. Use up to three singles and rest 4–6 minutes between attempts. Choose an opener recently completed cleanly at RPE 8 or easier. If warm-ups feel heavy, use the lighter route. For 160 → 170 → 175 kg, take the 10 kg first increase only if 160 is clearly comfortable (about RPE 7–7.5 or easier) and your recent work supports 170. Otherwise, if another attempt is warranted, use 160 → 165 → 170 kg. Take the final 5 kg only after a clean second with clear reserve. The stretch route requires a recently repeatable opener. End the session after a miss, a grind, loss of your usual technique or concerning symptoms. Log the heaviest completed single.Lighter route: 155 → 160 → 165 kg. Choose 155 kg only if it has been a repeatable, clean single at RPE 8 or easier in recent training. Rest 4–6 minutes between attempts. Each increase on this route is 5 kg. Take the next attempt only after a clean lift with clear reserve and when recent training supports it. End testing after a miss, a grind, loss of your usual technique or concerning symptoms. Record the heaviest successful single.Heavier route: 170 → 175 → 180 kg. Choose 170 kg only if it has been a repeatable, clean single at RPE 8 or easier in recent training. Rest 4–6 minutes between attempts. Each increase on this route is 5 kg. Take the next attempt only after a clean lift with clear reserve and when recent training supports it. End testing after a miss, a grind, loss of your usual technique or concerning symptoms. Record the heaviest successful single.

Choose your Thursday weight

30° low-incline barbell bench · 20 kg bar · 5 kg total steps

Start with a 45 kg trial after warming up. Use 40 kg if necessary for eight reps with two left. Keep the same weight until you can do 12 + 12 with at least two clean reps left. Then move one step to the right for your next regular session and aim for eight per set.

20 · 25 · 30 · 35 · 40 · 45 · 50 · 55 · 60 · 65 · 70 kg. Continue in 5 kg steps. To reduce the load, move one step to the left. Stay at or above the 20 kg empty bar.

A jump from 45 to 50 kg means adding one 2.5 kg plate to each side. If you can use 50 kg for the first eight only, use 45 kg for the second set and log both. After a benchmark Thursday, resume from the last regular session. A reduced rehearsal-week or taper set earns no load increase.
